issues.detail: The Hebrew says 'twelve for Benjamin and for Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twelve from the servants of David' — the Chinese renders '便雅憫' (Benjamin) and '掃羅的兒子伊施波設' (Ish-bosheth son of Saul) as separate groups, but the Hebrew has 'לְבִנְיָמִן וּלְאִישׁ בֹּשֶׁת בֶּן שָׁאוּל' meaning 'for Benjamin and for Ish-bosheth son of Saul' — these are two parties (Benjamin/Ish-bosheth vs. David's servants), not three. The Chinese adds a third group '大衛的僕人那裡也有十二人' as if it were a separate location, but the Hebrew only has two groups of twelve: twelve for Benjamin/Ish-bosheth and twelve from David's servants. The Chinese misconstrues the structure, making it appear there are three groups of twelve, whereas the Hebrew has two groups of twelve.
